objective: Decide whether counting colourings of cubic bipartite Pfaffian graphs under sign classes with branched twists (a square whose three branches are all twisted) is #P-hard, by realizing a crossover (exactly or by interpolation) from junctions of twisted pages and planar matchgate glue, or prove an obstruction to that route. Nearest known result: planar Holant and #CSP dichotomies (Cai-Lu-Xia, Guo-Williams, Cai-Fu-Guo-Williams), Jaeger-Vertigan-Welsh for the Ising line of the Tutte polynomial. Classification: to be decided.
status: Proved: a junction is never an exact crossover (its not-all-equal square lines carry no hard wire for nonnegative branch tensors; its points can), but twisted truncated-octahedron pages give soft crossings off the matchgate class, e.g. straight entries (40000, -1112, 3336, -192); hardness of branched twists by interpolation left open
title: Branched twists: can a junction cross wires?
